Goryopchagi is a technique used to perform kicks with the same leg two or more times in succession.
You usually strike an opponent's lower body, torso or face in succession.
Draw the attention of an opponent with the first kick, then dominate them with the second kick
or trip and block against an opponent's attack with the first kick and dominate them with the second kick.
Goryopchagi can be applied with various forms of kicks such as Goryopapchagi, Goryopyopchagi, Goryopdoryochagi, etc.
Chochojjirugi is a technique used to strike an opponent's lower abdomen downward
after pulling back the tip of the hand.
In Goryopumsae, Rullokkeokgi is a technique of using the arc fist, agmuson, downward
and holding an opponent's arm or leg with the other hand to press and twist.
You typically press and twist their joints to dominate them.
Besides pressing down and twisting the joints, another goal of Goryopumsae is to strike or push an opponent
by pressing, twisting their kneecap, disrupting their balance.
Palgumchiyopchigi is a technique that uses the edge of the elbow with the fist
and elbow in alignment to attack an opponent in a straight line from the inside out.
Sonnalbakkachigi is a technique that uses a reversed hand blade to attack from the inside out.
The target is an opponent's face and torso.
Sonnalaremakki is the same as aremakki, but it can also be used to strike and block an opponent's attack
by opening the hand, or used as baramakki and koramakki.
Agunsonapchigi is a technique typically used to attack an opponent's neck
with the arch of the arc fist and arm placed in a line.
To achieve a hard strike and prevent injuries, the wrist must be properly straightened.

Mejumokpyojeokarechigi is a technique used to slowly draw a circle with your arms, cross above your head.
Open your right hand in front of the lower abdomen,
then lightly hit your right palm with a left hammer fist.
The fist should be made at the shoulder line, slowly with a breath.
Naturally bend your arms.
Be careful not to straighten your wrists when your arms come down drawing a circle.

Anpalmokhaechomakki is a technique used to block inside out using the inner wrist of your arms.
The inner wrist should be level with your solar plexus when blocking defending the torso,
and the distance between the two should remain a shoulder's length.
Your elbow should face downward without detaching from the body,
and be careful the move does not resemble Deungjumokapchigi.
Sonnalyeopmakki is a technique to block the sides by performing Sonnalbakkanmakki
by standing sideways like standing in the Juchumseogi posture.
A reminder, the direction of the force progresses inside out.
The last of the 13 key moves is Pyojeokjirugi.
Pyojeokjirugi is a technique used to create a target with the palm of the hand.
Perform Jirugi toward the palm with the fist.
It is used to connect other techniques by pulling an opponent
using the force gathered in your hands after the Jirugi.
It is important to place the target and fist at the solar plexus level.
These are the 13 key moves of Goryeopumse.

Sonnal Aremakki is used not only for striking and blocking,
but also apply to Godomaki and Paramaki.
It is effective to block an opponent's inner or outer leg
when striking and blocking an opponent's attack.
The space between the thigh and the hand should be about two raised fists length.
Sonnal Aremakki and Agun Sonap-chigi are connected
and should be performed quickly in succession.
Ap-cha-ki and Sonnal Aremakki should connect without pause.
You need to control your breath to achieve a harmonious movement.
When blocking defending the torso,
your fists should be level with the solar plexus.
Remember that your fists should not rise above your shoulders.
Also, the left arm crosses outside the right foot if the left foot is in front,
and the right foot crosses outside the left foot if the right foot is in front.
Cautions for Koryo second part, taking a closer look.
Do not overextend the elbow of the blocking arm during the Sonnal Aremakki move.
Also, be careful not to rely solely on the strength of the arm to block.
During Ap-cha-ki, do not pause before the kick
or fold and raise the leg past the supporting leg to make the kick.
When performing Nullo-koki, the hand should not be above or below the elbow.
Do not use the palm of your hand with the wrist used to press and twist upward.
Concentrate force so that only the narrow part of the arc fist touches the target.
During Anpal-mok Hachomakki, do not cross your fists like Dung-jumok Ap-chigi
and turn forward on the inside.
Your center should not be on your hind leg during Ap-sugi.
